data.title: China Evergrande Strikes USD513 Million Deal to Offload Key Profitable Unit Amid Liquidation
data.description:
(Yicai) Oct. 30 -- China Evergrande Group, once China's largest property developer, has agreed to sell control of its property management arm to investment firm PAG for HKD4 billion (USD513.2 million), marking a major step in the liquidation of the debt-laden company.

The deal will see Hong Kong-based PAG acquire about 51 percent of Evergrande Property Services Group, one of the troubled developer's key remaining assets, advancing a sale process that began in September 2025 as liquidators sought to recover funds for China Evergrande's creditors.

China Evergrande and its subsidiary will sell all their shares in Evergrande Property at different prices, the Guangzhou-based property manager announced today. The weighted average transaction price is about HKD0.73 (9 US cents) per share, with the liquidators signing the share purchase agreement on behalf of the sellers.

Once the deal's conditions are met and the stake transfer is completed, PAG will become Evergrande Property's new controlling shareholder and launch a mandatory general offer for the remaining shares at HKD0.84 apiece, a nearly 30 percent discount to the stock's closing price before trading was suspended for one day yesterday.

PAG intends to “maintain the listing status of Evergrande Property” and has no plans to take the company private or delist it, the announcement said. However, whether the firm can remain listed will depend on the proportion of shares held by public investors after the offer closes.

Evergrande Property's shares tumbled after trading resumed today, closing 17.7 percent lower at HKD0.98. The company has a market capitalization of about HKD10.5 billion (USD1.3 billion).

PAG Expands Into Residential Property Services

PAG is an Asia-Pacific-focused alternative investment firm with more than USD60 billion in assets under management as of the end of June. Industry observers see the acquisition as a key step in expanding its real estate business from commercial properties into residential property management.

Evergrande Property was first put up for sale in 2021, when China Evergrande, then grappling with a liquidity crisis after years of rapid expansion fueled by borrowing, sought to raise cash by disposing of assets. The property management unit, which generated recurring revenue from managing residential communities, was among the group's key assets earmarked for sale.

China Evergrande's debt restructuring efforts subsequently ran into difficulties, and the Hong Kong High Court ordered the developer to be liquidated in January 2024. Responsibility for selling Evergrande Property then passed to the liquidators.

Despite its parent's financial collapse, Evergrande Property has remained profitable. Its revenue rose almost 5 percent from a year earlier to CNY6.9 billion (USD1 billion) in the first half of this year, while profit attributable to shareholders climbed about 10 percent to CNY517 million (USD77.6 million).

As of the end of June, Evergrande Property had about CNY4.2 billion (USD637 million) in available funds and virtually no interest-bearing debt.

Editor: Emmi Laine

data.title: Global Data Ecosystem Conference in Shanghai Hears About Int’l Digital Cooperation, Data-AI Integration
data.description:
(Yicai) Oct. 30 -- The main forum of the Global Data Ecosystem Conference 2026 was held in Shanghai today, with industry experts and business leaders discussing international digital collaboration and the integration of data and artificial intelligence.

Under the theme of “Data Intelligence Connecting the World,” the conference also unveiled new initiatives, and discussed efforts to boost the practical use of data technologies across various industries.

During the opening ceremony, the China Meteorological Administration introduced two key initiatives: The Shanghai Node for International Exchange of Earth System Data and Trusted Data Space for the Meteorological Industry. These achievements are expected to empower smart city development and support the high-quality growth of the digital economy.

In addition, the Working Group for the World Data Organization Maritime and Trade Digitization Specialized Committee was officially established. Building on Shanghai’s strengths in shipping and trade, the group is expected to support the smart upgrading of port and trade operations.

Song Xianrong, director of the International Data Governance Cooperation Department of the National Data Administration, and Wu Jianxiong, chairman of Shanghai Data Group, attended the launch ceremony.

The conference also officially launched the China-Kazakhstan Industrial Cooperation in Digital Economy initiative through which the two countries will collaborate in areas including digital economy industry research, co-development of cross-border digital infrastructure, smart city construction, and the development of data factor markets.

Moreover, the conference held an awards ceremony for the Shanghai regional leg of the 2026 Data Elements × Competition (a national contest aimed at unlocking the multiplier effect of data as a production factor). The event in Shanghai covered 20 major categories, including meteorological services, manufacturing, financial services, green and low-carbon development, and healthcare, with 143 teams receiving awards. The winning projects will be supported in moving from the competition stage into real-world industrial applications.

The Token Industry Ecosystem Synergy Initiative was also unveiled by the National Data Development Research Institute, a research institute directly under China's National Data Administration, and several leading companies across the industry chain. The initiative aims to advance the development of standards, evaluation, and practical application scenarios for the "token" sector, while forging new pathways for measuring, pricing, and circulating data — with the AI token as the unit of account — in the era of large AI models.

Experts Discuss Emerging Industry Trends

At the main forum, Sun Shengli, a member of the Chinese Academy of Sciences, delivered a speech on specialized data center architecture and sustainable ecology as well as the underlying support path for scientific data mining and utilization.

A representative from Kazakhstan shared the country’s experience in developing the digital economy, opening up new perspectives for digital cooperation with China. Joe Weinman, founder of the International Institute for Future Industries and a pioneer in AI economics, analyzed industry transformation driven by data.

Vincenzo Aquaro, Chief of Digital Government Branch in UN DESA’s Division for Public Institutions and Digital Government, focused on the era of AI agents and shared cutting-edge research on the global development of digital government.

Wu Jianxiong, chairman of Shanghai Data Group, said the firm will build an open, shared and mutually beneficial platform for communication, engage deeply in the reform of data as a factor of production, and work alongside industry partners to foster the coordinated development of data resources.

Technological and Industrial Innovations Unveiled

During the forum, a carbon footprint certification chain for recyclable materials was launched. By leveraging data capabilities, this system enables end-to-end traceability and management of recyclable materials, empowering the circular economy to scale up and standardize.

UniTrust, a trusted governance platform for AI agents developed by the Shanghai Electronic Certificate Authority Center, was also unveiled. The platform is intended to establish a foundational layer of digital trust to ensure the secure and reliable circulation of data factors.

In addition, the first batch of high-quality datasets from AIsaisi, a one-stop open community for AI-driven scientific research, was released, providing data resources to support cutting-edge scientific research and innovation.

The National Data Development Research Institute, Shanghai Data Group, and Shanghai Data Research Institute also jointly released a series of research findings on the integrated development of blockchain, data, and AI.

Editor: Tom Litting

data.title: [Exclusive] Beijing Hyundai’s First Chinese General Manager to Exit After Just One Year
data.description:
(Yicai) Oct. 30 -- Li Fenggang, the first Chinese national to serve as general manager of Beijing Hyundai Motor, the 50:50 joint venture between China’s BAIC Motor and South Korea’s Hyundai Motor, will step down on Nov. 1, one year after taking up the role, Yicai learned today from company insiders.

Li’s departure is more than a routine management change, a source familiar with the matter told Yicai. Behind his exit lie disagreements between Beijing Hyundai’s Chinese and South Korean shareholders over the JV’s future development path.

Over the past year, the two shareholders have failed to reach consensus on key issues including business targets and cost-cutting goals, the source said. This has stalled efforts to deepen the firm’s localization reforms. As Beijing Hyundai’s first Chinese general manager, Li, who previously worked for FAW-Volkswagen and FAW Audi Sales, found himself at the center of these tensions.

Under the JV’s established organizational structure, the general manager of Beijing Hyundai is appointed by the South Korean shareholder and is usually held by a South Korean national, while the executive deputy general manager is appointed by BAIC. Li’s appointment as the firm’s first Chinese general manager was widely seen at the time as part of Hyundai Motor Global Chief Executive Officer José Muñoz’s efforts to localize the management team.

However, according to people familiar with the matter, South Korean nationals continue to dominate key positions within the management structure appointed by the South Korean shareholder. In practice, Li’s authority over resource allocation and business decision-making did not match the seniority implied by his title. The underlying strategic differences and lack of mutual trust between the two shareholders were issues beyond the management team’s ability to resolve.

Disagreements between shareholders in a JV can greatly undermine operational efficiency. At Beijing Hyundai, the differences first became apparent in discussions over annual targets, with the Chinese and South Korean shareholders struggling for a long time to reach an agreement.

It was not until September this year that the two sides finally reached a new consensus, setting an annual sales target of about 160,000 vehicles and aiming to keep losses at around CNY1.9 billion (USD285 million).

Li’s departure has brought the issue of Beijing Hyundai’s failure to localize decision-making authority into sharper focus. Although the Chinese and South Korean shareholders have now reached a temporary agreement on the company’s operating targets, how the JV will move forward remains to be seen.

Editor: Kim Taylor

data.title: Chinese Cancer Drugmakers Raise Global Stakes With Record Oncology Congress Showing
data.description:
(Yicai) Oct. 28 -- A record 29 Chinese innovative cancer drug studies were selected to showcase new findings at a leading global oncology conference, highlighting the country's growing ability to develop treatments that could change clinical practice worldwide.

The number of Chinese studies selected as late-breaking abstracts (LBAs) surged to 29 at this year's European Society for Medical Oncology (ESMO) Congress in Madrid, Spain, from just seven in 2024, Yicai learned from Chinese participants at the event, which concluded yesterday. Of the 29 studies, 20 presented Phase III clinical trial results. Five were selected for the Presidential Symposium, which showcases the conference's most significant findings, compared with none in 2024.

The ESMO Congress is one of Europe's leading cancer research conferences, where drugmakers unveil major clinical breakthroughs. Its LBAs highlight potentially practice-changing findings vetted through international peer review. Chinese studies accounted for about one-third of the more than 90 LBAs selected this year, a record-high proportion.

The selected studies involved drug developers including Hutchmed, Keymed Biosciences, Lepu Biopharma, Akeso, Hansoh Pharmaceutical Group, and Kelun-Biotech Biopharmaceutical, covering lung, gastrointestinal, and gynecological cancers.

Shift to Late-Stage Clinical Trials

Beyond the record number and share of selections, Chinese drugmakers are also making progress in the maturity of their research.

In previous years, most Chinese studies presented at the congress involved exploratory findings from early-stage Phase I and Phase II trials. This year, Phase III results dominated, marking a shift toward large-scale trials that typically precede regulatory approval.

The results suggest that China's innovative oncology drugs are moving beyond early proof-of-concept research toward randomized controlled trials capable of generating evidence that could change clinical practice, Xiangcai Securities said.

The brokerage noted that LBAs prioritize randomized Phase II and Phase III clinical trials and have stringent selection criteria. The growing body of late-stage evidence could accelerate updates to international treatment guidelines, overseas licensing deals, and commercialization.

Editor: Emmi Laine

data.title: China’s E-Town Reports Solid Third-Quarter Earnings, Unveils USD270 Million Gear Capacity Expansion
data.description:
(Yicai) Oct. 30 -- E-Town Semiconductor Technology, a leading Chinese semiconductor equipment firm, has announced strong earnings for the third quarter of the year and a CNY1.8 billion (USD270.4 million) investment in a new factory.

Revenue rose 10 percent to CNY1.5 billion in the three months ended Sept. 30 from a year earlier, while net profit quadrupled to CNY677 million (USD101.7 million), the Beijing-based firm said in its latest financial statement yesterday.

Net profit excluding non-recurring items widened 16 percent to CNY184 million (USD 27.41 million), E-Town noted, adding that non-recurring gains mainly came from fair-value changes of equity investments.

In the first three quarters of the year, E-Town reported a 5.6 percent decline in revenue to CNY3.6 billion, while its net profit surged 108 percent to CNY1.1 billion. Net profit excluding non-recurring items inched up 3.4 percent to CNY427 million.

In a separate statement yesterday, E-Town said it plans to build a new semiconductor equipment manufacturing plant in the Beijing Economic-Technological Development Area to mass-produce a range of self-developed semiconductor tools, including dry strip systems, rapid thermal processing systems, dry etch systems, and plasma surface treatment systems.

The project is expected to lift the company’s in-house manufacturing capacity and delivery efficiency, better meet client demand, and boost profitability, E-Town noted, without revealing any further details.

E-Town develops, manufactures, and sells wafer processing equipment for chip fabrication, supplying dry strip, rapid thermal processing, dry etch, and plasma surface treatment systems with supporting process solutions to global fabs, including leading memory and logic chipmakers. Its first manufacturing plant in Beijing started operation in 2018.

E-Town’s shares [SHA: 688729] closed 1.9 percent up at CNY17.39 (USD2.61) apiece in Shanghai today, after earlier gaining as much as 7.7 percent.

Editor: Futura Costaglione

data.title: China's Li Auto Uses Only Self-Developed Batteries, Smart-Driving Chips in New i6 Model
data.description:
(Yicai) Oct. 30 -- Li Auto has used only self-developed batteries and smart-driving chips in the 2026 edition of its i6, the Chinese electric vehicle startup's best-selling model.

Li Auto changed the battery in the new i6 from one co-developed with Contemporary Amperex Technology to its own Lianshan 5C battery, which offers improved capacity and endurance. It also replaced Nvidia's Thor-U smart-driving chip with its M100 chip.

The move highlights that Li Auto's self-developed core components are transitioning from small-batch validation to large-scale use. The Beijing-based firm has delivered nearly 190,000 i6 battery EVs since launching the model at the end of September last year.

According to data from the China Passenger Car Association, Li Auto delivered 160,221 i6s in the nine months ended Sept. 30, accounting for about 55 percent of its total deliveries. Among all pure electric sport utility vehicles priced above CNY200,000 (USD30,025), the i6 ranked second in sales behind Tesla's Model Y with 277,290 units.

The i6 is also a frontier product in Li Auto's global expansion. Known as Li 6 overseas, the model will launch in Norway and the Netherlands in the first quarter of next year, before gradually expanding to other European markets.

Li Xiang, chairman and chief executive officer of Li Auto, previously said he hopes the i6 will be the firm's best-selling model worldwide.

Since the i6 2026 launch, Morgan Stanley has maintained an Overweight rating on Li Auto with a target price of HKD68.50 (USD8.73) a share and believes the new model will likely boost the firm's monthly sales to 15,000 to 20,000 units from around 7,000 units last month.

However, sales growth will depend on whether Li Auto's self-developed battery and chip supply can keep up with orders and the order conversion rate, Morgan Stanley stressed. The car's fourth-quarter sales gross profit margin and sales data will be key to whether the company's long-term vehicle gross profit margin can reach its 15 percent target, it added.

Editors: Tang Shihua, Martin Kadiev

data.title: Global Healthcare Firms to Showcase New Drugs, AI Scanners at CIIE
data.description:
(Yicai) Oct. 30 -- Global pharmaceutical companies and medical device makers will showcase new drugs, artificial intelligence-powered diagnostic equipment, and surgical systems, and highlight their local manufacturing capabilities at the upcoming China International Import Expo.

Themed ‘Healthy China, Healthy Life,’ the healthcare section of the ninth CIIE, which will kick off in Shanghai on Nov. 5, will cover pharmaceuticals, medical devices, health and nutrition, and elderly care. It will feature 12 drugmakers on the Fortune Global 500 list, 16 of the world's 20 largest pharmaceutical companies, and all three leading firms in medical imaging and radiotherapy.

Takeda Pharmaceutical will showcase oveporexton, an oral treatment for type 1 narcolepsy that received its first global regulatory approval in China in July.

Boehringer Ingelheim will bring verducatib, an investigational treatment for bronchiectasis in Phase III clinical development, Caninebeat AI, a tool that helps veterinarians detect heart murmurs associated with structural heart disease in dogs, and Senvelgo, an oral solution for treating feline diabetes.

Gilead Sciences, which is attending the CIIE for the fifth consecutive year, expects lenacapavir for the prevention of human immunodeficiency virus, as well as liver disease drug seladelpar, to receive formal regulatory approval in China soon, the US biopharmaceutical company said on Oct. 26.

Lenacapavir was approved in China in January 2025 to treat adults with multidrug-resistant HIV-1, while its use for HIV prevention is only available through a special-access program in Hainan's Boao Lecheng International Medical Tourism Pilot Zone. Seladelpar, a treatment for primary biliary cholangitis, is available through special-access programs in Boao Lecheng and Beijing's Tianzhu Comprehensive Bonded Zone.

"The CIIE is not only a platform to showcase global innovations but also an important link connecting innovation, collaboration, and patients' needs," said Jin Fangqian, Gilead's vice president and China general manager.

Bayer will bring to the CIIE Sunharbo, the world's first approved factor XIa inhibitor, having received Chinese regulatory clearance on Oct. 26. Other Bayer exhibits include lung cancer drug Hyrnuo, which has received Chinese approval, and the Medrad Mark 7 Arterion high-pressure contrast injection system, which is made in China and has obtained domestic medical device registration.

Medical device makers will showcase new imaging and surgical technologies at the CIIE. Royal Philips will display 10 products, including the BlueSeal Horizon, a 3T magnetic resonance imaging system that it describes as “the world's first helium-free model of its class.” The MRI system remains under development and is not yet commercially available.

Moreover, Philips will bring its Verida CT scanner, an AI-powered, detector-based spectral computed tomography system that has received regulatory clearance in the United States.

Siemens Healthineers will debut its Naeotom Alpha.Peak photon-counting CT scan in China, while GE HealthCare will showcase its Photonova Spectra photon-counting CT scanner in the country for the first time.

Exhibitors are also highlighting their manufacturing and research capabilities in China. Siemens Healthineers received regulatory approval in June for its first China-made photon-counting CT scanner, the Naetom Alpha.Pro, which will be manufactured at its production base in Shanghai's Zhangjiang High-Tech Park.

Intuitive Fosun, a joint venture between Chinese drugmaker Fosun Pharmaceutical and US biotech firm Intuitive Surgical, will showcase a China-made da Vinci Xi surgical robot. Shanghai is Intuitive’s only production site for da Vinci robots outside the US.

Editor: Futura Costaglione

data.title: China's Kung Fu-Inspired AAA Game Phantom Blade Zero Tops Steam Charts on Release
data.description:
(Yicai) Oct. 30 -- Phantom Blade Zero, a Chinese AAA action game inspired by the choreography of Hong Kong kung fu films, shot to the top of the global best-selling chart of digital distribution platform Steam on its first day, with its success likened to Game Science's 2024 hit Black Myth: Wukong.

Beijing-based S-Game launched Phantom Blade Zero on Windows and Sony's PlayStation 5 yesterday, with concurrent players on Steam surpassing 300,000 within an hour before peaking at 723,876.

The game builds a fictional world that blends elements of wuxia -- a Chinese literary genre centered on martial arts heroes, chivalry, and justice -- with steampunk aesthetics. Players take on the role of a swordsman whose heart has been badly damaged and who has only 66 days left to live, unraveling a conspiracy that shrouds the martial arts world.

To make the wuxia adventure work, the creative team invested substantial resources, said Liang Qiwei, founder and chief executive officer of S-Game. The project's development cost was between CNY300 million and CNY400 million (USD45.1 million and USD60.1 million), close to that of Black Myth: Wukong, Liang pointed out.

Tech giant Tencent Holdings is one of S-Game's key investors and has also provided key funding and resource support for Phantom Blade Zero's AAA development, indicating a high-budget, high-profile game developer, and a well-known publisher. ZhenFund, NetEase Capital, and Hero Entertainment were also among the studio's early investors.

Compared with Black Myth: Wukong, which broke into the market by leveraging Chinese classical mythology and the Monkey King intellectual property, Phantom Blade Zero focuses on showcasing wuxia combat, Zhang Shule, a game industry analyst, told Yicai. The new game is more of a steampunk-styled wuxia game with an aesthetic reminiscent of the Best Foreign Film Oscar-winner Crouching Tiger, Hidden Dragon, so it may attract more overseas players, Zhang pointed out.

It would be difficult for Phantom Blade Zero to match the sales of Black Myth: Wukong, but reaching 10 million copies sold in its first year looks very promising, a game industry investor said to Yicai, noting that its content is "distinctive and well polished."

The game's pre-order numbers have been solid, allowing it to build sales momentum, an industry insider pointed out. The next question is whether word of mouth can sustain continued sales, the person noted, adding that if it eventually reaches even half the sales of Black Myth: Wukong's, or around 15 million, that would be a huge success.

Phantom Blade Zero's pre-orders topped 500,000 as of Oct. 20, bringing in revenue of about USD24 million, according to data analytics site Alinea Analytics. In the 70 days before its release, Phantom Blade Zero sales were about 73 percent of Black Myth: Wukong's in the same period.

Black Myth: Wukong changed the external environment for Chinese standalone games, an insider from the game publishing sector told Yicai. Players are willing to pay for premium domestic single-player games, while leading publishers have increased investment in such titles, with the industry as a whole stepping up spending on development and marketing, which has attracted more professionals to join, the person stressed.

A batch of single-player game projects launched by developers over the past few years is expected to enter a peak release period over the next two years, the insider pointed out. Who will be the next Black Myth: Wukong may no longer be the key question as more titles launch, he said, noting that what matters more is that games across genres must find enough players and investment returns to fund the development of the next title, creating a healthy industry cycle.

Editors: Tang Shihua, Martin Kadiev

data.title: Volkswagen China Unveils New Integrated Tech Stack
data.description:
(Yicai) Oct. 30 -- Volkswagen China has launched VEGA, an integrated technology stack developed by the Chinese team of the German auto giant, making it the only foreign carmaker in the country with a complete in-house tech matrix.

Volkswagen China's local engineering team spearheaded the development of VEGA, which comprises three core components: Compact Main Platform, China Electronic Architecture, and advanced driver-assistance systems, the company announced on Oct. 28. The parent firm is accelerating the rollout of China-developed technologies to more overseas markets, with plans to initially deploy the solution in South America by 2030, followed by expansions to South Africa and others.

The deep integration of the CMP and CEA will serve as the technical foundation for Volkswagen Group's next-generation model development targeting the Global South markets, as its China strategy evolves from "in China, for China" to "in China, and beyond." VEGA will enable local customized development and support multiple powertrain options, including new energy, internal combustion, and hybrid systems.

"China is a key innovation engine for Volkswagen and increasingly a product and tech hub for our global markets," noted Chief Executive Oliver Blume.

The launch of VEGA also marks a large-scale transfer of product decision-making and definition authority from Volkswagen's headquarters to the Chinese unit. The move aims to recapture market share in China, where its footprint has shrunk in recent years, and harness mature vehicle development tech and a supply chain infrastructure refined in the country to seize new growth opportunities in emerging Global South markets.

Editors: Tang Shihua, Martin Kadiev

data.title: ByteDance's Short Drama Platform Hongguo Becomes China's Fourth-Largest App; Douyin VP Addresses Quality Concerns
data.description:
(Yicai) Oct. 30 -- Hongguo, a short drama platform under ByteDance, has climbed to fourth in China by time spent per user, boosted by the soaring popularity of the new entertainment form in the country, while the vice president of the Chinese internet giant's short-video arm Douyin doubled down on content quality at the core amid growing online concerns.

Hongguo accounted for 5 percent of the time Chinese users spend using apps in July, ranking behind only TikTok's sister app Douyin at 19.4 percent, Tencent Holdings' super app WeChat at 18.8 percent, and Douyin Express Edition at 6.3 percent, according to the latest data from QuestMobile. In addition, its daily active users more than doubled to 168 million in the same month from a year ago, exceeding the combined total of video platforms Tencent Video, iQiyi, Youku, and Mango TV.

The rapid growth of the short drama market has also attracted more entrants. Monthly active users of Lvpaopao, a new short drama mini-program housed within WeChat, reached almost 90 million in the first week of this month, up 44 percent from the first week of September and compared with 143 million for the whole of August, QuestMobile data showed.

Douyin VP Li Liang said on Weibo yesterday that there is no essential difference between short dramas and traditional films and television series, responding to online concerns after Hongguo became the fourth-largest app in China.

As technology develops, artificial intelligence is expected to open up new innovative space in short drama production, especially in historical and science fiction genres, where it can create scenes at a lower cost that are difficult to achieve with traditional production methods, Li stressed. The creativity level will likely continue to improve and approach the production level of Hollywood blockbusters, Li said.

Editor: Martin Kadiev

data.title: Food, Tobacco, and Liquor Account for Nearly a Third of China’s Per Capita Consumption Last Year
data.description:
(Yicai) Oct. 30 -- Chinese residents splurged almost one-third of their total consumer spending on food, tobacco, and liquor last year, according to data compiled by Yicai.

China’s per capita consumption spending stood at CNY29,476 (USD4,426) in 2025, Yicai calculated based on data from the China Statistical Yearbook 2026. Among that, CNY8,631 (USD1,296) was spent on food, tobacco, and liquor, up 2.6 percent from 2024 and accounting for over 29 percent of the total.

Eight provincial-level regions -- Shanghai, Zhejiang province, Guangdong province, Fujian province, Jiangsu province, Tianjin, Beijing, and Hainan province -- had per capita spending on food, tobacco, and liquor above CNY10,000.

Meanwhile, 12 provincial-level regions -- Hainan, Xizang Autonomous Region, Anhui province, Guangdong, Fujian, Sichuan province, Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region, Chongqing, Jiangxi province, Yunnan province, Guangxi province, and Qinghai province -- had food, tobacco, and liquor spending exceeding 30 percent of the total. Hainan ranked first at 37 percent, and Guangdong ranked fourth at 32 percent.

Overall, southern provinces spend somewhat more on food, thanks to warmer weather and a livelier nightlife.

China’s per capita spending on housing rose 2.1 percent to CNY6,397 last year from 2024, accounting for nearly 22 percent of the total per capita consumption expenditure, down from about 19 percent in 2020.

Beijing, Shanghai, Fujian, Jiangsu, Guangdong, and Zhejiang had the six highest shares of housing spending to the total consumption expenditure, and they are all in East China.

Transportation and communication took another big chunk of household consumption. China’s per capita spending on transportation and communication averaged CNY4,306 in 2025, up 8.3 percent from the year before and accounting for 15 percent of the total.

Inner Mongolia Autonomous Region and Qinghai had the highest percentages, as their sparse population and dispersed settlements raised related costs. Beijing and Shanghai had lower percentages of about 11 percent, as both cities have well-developed public transport, and their relatively high incomes allow more spending in other areas.

Per capita spending on healthcare rose 1 percent to CNY2,573 yuan in 2025 from the previous year, accounting for 8.7 percent of the total per capita consumption expenditure. Heilongjiang province had the highest share of over 13 percent. Northeast China, where the population is relatively older, has a higher share of healthcare spending.

Editor: Futura Costaglione

data.title: CATL Globally Launches Tener+ Energy Storage System, Debuts Tener Sodium in Australia to Tackle Extreme Climates
data.description:
(Yicai) Oct. 29 -- China's Contemporary Amperex Technology has globally launched a new ultra-high-capacity energy storage system and showcased its sodium-ion battery storage technology in Australia for the first time, aiming to meet demand for reliable energy storage in extreme weather conditions.

The world's largest electric vehicle battery manufacturer unveiled its new-generation lithium-ion battery storage system Tener+ and exhibited its Tener Sodium system at All Energy Australia 2026, a major renewable energy and clean technology exhibition, yesterday.

CATL also signed separate memorandums of understanding with Zurich-based Hitachi Energy, Australia's EPEC Group, and the University of New South Wales during the exhibition, covering grid connection, system integration, and talent development, respectively.

Both Tener+ and Tener Sodium are designed to meet Australia's stringent grid connection requirements and support the long-term performance and profitability of energy storage projects, the Ningde-based company said.

Tener+ has a 25-year design lifespan and packs about 9 megawatt-hours of direct-current storage capacity into a single 20-foot container, making it ideal for space-constrained projects. Its intelligent thermal management system allows the power conversion system to operate at full rated power even in extreme summer heat.

Tener Sodium is the world's first mass-produced and field-proven sodium-ion battery energy storage system, according to CATL. With a capacity exceeding 30 MWh per system, it operates in temperatures from minus 35 to 55 degrees Celsius and delivers more than 10,000 charge-discharge cycles at 45 degrees Celsius, making it suitable for Australia's hot climate.

Focus on Long-Term Performance

According to Zane Zhou, general manager of CATL Australia and New Zealand, both systems are designed to meet developers' needs for long-term battery performance, reliable charge-discharge cycles, and participation in Australia's National Electricity Market, the country's main wholesale electricity market.

Zhou added that offering both sodium-ion and lithium-ion technologies gives asset owners and project developers greater flexibility to choose the most suitable solution for their projects.

CATL has ranked first globally in energy storage battery shipments for five consecutive years, with a market share of 30.4 percent in 2025, according to SNE Research. The company has delivered more than 3,000 energy storage projects worldwide, with cumulative installed capacity in Australia exceeding 17 gigawatt-hours.

Editor: Emmi Laine

data.title: Chinese EV Giant BYD Enters Namibian Market in Global Expansion Drive
data.description:
(Yicai) Oct. 7 -- Chinese automaker BYD has officially launched its new energy vehicle brand in Namibia, expanding its presence in the African market.

Namibian automotive distributor Pupkewitz Motors announced yesterday that it will represent BYD in the country, with the brand to be offered through retail outlets in Windhoek, Walvis Bay and Ongwediva.

"Our ambition is not simply to introduce new vehicles to the market, but to create an experience around new energy mobility that is relevant to Namibian customers. We look forward to building awareness, educating consumers and allowing customers to experience BYD for themselves," said Nico Pieters, a franchise executive at Pupkewitz Motors, in a statement.

Models being introduced to the Namibian market include the BYD Dolphin, BYD Dolphin Surf, BYD Sealion 5, BYD Sealion 6, BYD Shark 6, BYD Sealion 7 and BYD Seal Performance.

"The range allows Namibian customers to explore different forms of electrified mobility while experiencing the technology, comfort and features associated with the BYD brand," Pieters said.

He said the launch comes as energy efficiency, sustainability and the future of transportation gain increasing attention globally.

"BYD's global focus on new energy technologies places the brand at the forefront of this changing automotive landscape, while its entry into Namibia provides local motorists with greater access to alternative vehicle technologies," he added.

With the official launch of BYD, Pupkewitz Motors is expanding its portfolio to include a global new energy vehicle brand, reinforcing its commitment to providing Namibian customers with greater choice as mobility evolves.

In September, economic and market indicators from Namibian firm IJG Securities, showed that Chinese brands are steadily gaining popularity in Namibia. Haval, Jetour and Chery accounted for 5.9 percent, 5.8 percent and 2.3 percent, respectively, of the Namibian passenger vehicle market.

Editor: Dou Shicong

data.title: Innovation Is China's Main Draw for Foreign Patients Over Cheaper Asian Rivals, Insiders Say
data.description:
(Yicai) Oct. 29 -- Advanced treatments, medical devices, and other healthcare innovation are the main pull for foreign patients coming to China for treatment, though the country cannot match other Asian countries on price, according to several insiders.

Most foreign patients come to China for advanced treatments such as chimeric antigen receptor-T cell therapy, with price just one consideration, Men Shaohua, operations director at the Children's Hospital of Fudan University, said at a forum hosted by healthcare provider SinoUnited Health in Shanghai on Oct. 26. Treatment costs in Thailand are about a third lower than in China, with those in India down a further third, he estimates.

SinoUnited Health has treated more than 40 overseas CAR-T cell therapy patients from 12 countries and regions at an estimated cost of one-third to one-quarter that in the United States, founder and Chief Executive Kathy Shi pointed out. 

At the forum, SinoUnited Health officially launched its international pan-vascular second medical opinion service, covering cardiovascular, cerebrovascular and peripheral vascular conditions, as well as metabolic and systemic risks. The service offers medical record reviews, remote multidisciplinary consultations, treatment coordination, English-language post-treatment reports and wearable-device-based follow-up after patients return home.

Demand keeps growing, with Li Feng, founder and CEO of cross-border medical services platform Yilian Medical, who has 15 years of experience in inbound medical services, said that he received a message from a Malaysian patient seeking surgery at the forum.

From Cases to Devices

China's large caseloads also feed into device development, with Zhongshan Hospital performing more aortic dissection procedures than any other hospital worldwide, having a patient cohort of more than 7,000, said Chief Physician of Vascular Surgery Fu Weiguo.

The volume helped reveal a problem others had missed, with some patients dying suddenly after receiving stent grafts, Fu noted, adding that the grafts could rub against the swollen aortic wall, causing a new tear. Foreign stents were designed for aneurysms, where the wall is largely normal, he said.

Fu's team published the finding in Circulation in 2009 and worked with manufacturers on design changes, including tapered stents. Several companies, including US-based Gore, also reduced the spring-back force of their stents, Fu pointed out.

Fu also turned clinical needs into tools. Inspired by a gastroscope that bends 360 degrees, he worked with Shenzhen-based Lifetech Scientific for eight years to develop the FuStar steerable sheath, which has 510(k) clearance from the US Food and Drug Administration. 

The team and Lifetech later developed Futhrough, which punctures a stent graft to reopen the subclavian artery and spares patients a bypass operation, with no comparable product existing before, according to Fu. Foreign doctors training at Zhongshan were more interested in specialized tools such as steerable sheaths and puncture needles than in stents, which are widely available, he added.

In addition, Pan Wenzhi, a cardiologist at Zhongshan Hospital, developed ValveClamp, the world's first transapical mitral valve clip, and RunFlow, China's first aortic valve dilation balloon that does not require interrupting blood flow. Both are already available on the market, while ReAces, the world's first atrial septal occluder that can be punctured through, has been submitted for approval.

Capital and policy support help accelerate medical device development and commercialization, Pan said. “Without them, we could only make small samples in our labs to play around with. There would be no way to commercialize them.”

Remaining Hurdles

However, barriers remain. Not every foreigner can afford treatment, said Chen Dan, director of Zhongshan Hospital's international medical department.

Payment terms are another hurdle, the head of a European federation of overseas Chinese medical and health groups pointed out. Foreign insurers are used to monthly settlement, while major Chinese hospitals ask for deposits up front, creating friction in payment arrangements, the person added.

In addition, information is inconsistent, with some new service providers using artificial intelligence to generate inbound medical websites, a few of which get Chinese hospital names wrong, said Li Feng, founder of cross-border medical platform Zhiyuan Yilian. Needs also differ by market -- Southeast Asian patients focus on budget, while those from Europe and the US scrutinize what a price quote does and does not cover, Li added.

Inbound medical services represent the image of Chinese healthcare and should not be treated as a get-rich-quick business, Li stressed.

Editor: Martin Kadiev

data.title: Chengdu Marathon Disqualifies Two Pacers for Changing Clothing as 'Battle for Runners' Feet' Intensifies in China
data.description:
(Yicai) Oct. 29 -- The Chengdu Marathon Organizing Committee disqualified two pacers for illegally changing their clothes and shoes during the city's latest marathon, highlighting the growing rivalry in the commercialization of Chinese marathons.

The two pacers, who are experienced runners tasked with running at a specific speed to set the pace for the marathon, received a two-year ban and had their pacer qualifications revoked, the committee announced on Oct. 27. The Chinese Athletics Association has been notified, it stressed.

According to online reports, the two pacers started the marathon wearing clothes and shoes from Chinese sportswear maker Li-Ning, the top sponsor of the Chengdu Marathon this season, before switching to two other brands during the race. There has been no confirmation of whether the two were paid, but the move signals that the "battle for runners' feet" has become so intense that brands compete even for ordinary runners.

The Chengdu Marathon Organizing Committee did not name any brands.

A high-level marathon has dozens of pacers and tens of thousands of runners, so the more people wear a brand's products, the more exposure it gains. At the same time, the number of sponsorship slots has shrunk amid a decline in marathons in China over the past two years, making top events scarce entry points for brands to seize.

The sponsorship map of Chinese marathons has changed drastically. Xtep International Holdings has run events for nearly 20 years, sponsoring 74 major events since its first marathon in 2007, including supporting the Xiamen marathon for the 17th consecutive year in 2025.

Xtep reported revenue rose 4.2 percent to CNY14.2 billion (USD2.1 billion) last year from the previous year, with that of its main brand rising only 1.5 percent. Its footwear income jumped 4.5 percent to CNY8.4 billion (USD1.3 billion).

However, Li-Ning has been gaining market share, with the running category growing in importance for the firm in recent years. Running business revenue accounted for 31 percent of its total income last year, up from 16 percent five years ago, surpassing basketball as the largest category, according to its financial reports. Starting this year, Li-Ning replaced Xtep as the top partner of the Chengdu marathon for the next five years, making it the first top event in Southwest China the company has been tied to.

In addition, On, Hoka, and Salomon are attracting middle-class urban runners by opening flagship stores, hosting running events, and holding community operations rather than sponsoring races.

Although marathons remain popular in China, the number of events continues to decline as organizers focus resources on top-tier events. Marathons and related road-running events nationwide fell to 594 last year from a record high of 696 in 2024, while the figure will likely drop to 492 this year, according to data from the Chinese Athletics Association.

Editor: Martin Kadiev

data.title: Schneider Electric’s Biggest Medium-Voltage Equipment Base Goes Live in China’s Xiamen
data.description:
(Yicai) Oct. 29 -- French energy technology leader Schneider Electric has put the first phase of its largest medium-voltage electrical equipment facility into operation in Xiamen, China's southeastern Fujian province, integrating a research and development tech center and a smart manufacturing and service training center.

The base, covering nearly 110,000 square meters and with a total investment of about CNY1.2 billion (USD180.2 million), became operational yesterday, Schneider Electric announced on the same day. Construction on the second phase has also kicked off.

The facility is equipped with Schneider Electric's most advanced customized production line for medium-voltage switchgear, a sheet metal workshop, an automatic copper bar production line, and multiple intelligent test equipment, the Rueil-based company pointed out.

The largest single steel structure span in the first phase is 37 meters, six times that of a regular plant, capable of withstanding category 17 typhoons, the head of the base pointed out.

Based on upgraded manufacturing and operational models in the first phase, the second phase will further expand capabilities in key tech processes and core licenses, focusing on producing vacuum arc extinguishing chambers, medium voltage circuit breakers, and other products, according to official sources in Xiamen, citing Xu Shaofeng, senior vice president of Schneider Electric.

Editor: Martin Kadiev

data.title: WeRide's Physical AI Infrastructure Unit Jingshuo Raises Over USD10 Million in First Fundraiser
data.description:
(Yicai) Oct. 29 -- Jingshuo, the physical artificial intelligence data and model infrastructure subsidiary of Chinese self-driving firm WeRide, has raised CNY70 million (USD10.5 million) in its first external financing round.

The pre-Series A fundraiser, which boasted investors such as Vision Knight Capital, Hong Kong Science and Technology Parks, and Sirius Capital, values the company at CNY2.07 billion (USD310.7 million), the Guangzhou-based company told Yicai today.

The proceeds will be used to expand Jingshuo’s core research and development team, integrate its data platform, world model, and skill asset engine, and broaden the tasks and scenarios covered by its datasets, the firm noted.

Jingshuo’s products include Egok, a high-precision first-person data collection device, as well as large-scale data collection, datasets, and customized data services, all built on its in-house WorldEngine data and model platform and Genesis-Robotics generative world model.

Jingshuo works with dozens of foundation model and embodied AI companies and has more than 100 customers and ecosystem partners. Its unaudited revenue was about CNY187 million (USD27.8 million) last year.

The company has about CNY1 billion worth of orders in hand, including formal contracts and confirmed customer orders that have yet to be fulfilled or recognized as revenue, it told Yicai.

WeRide established Jingshuo in May 2024 to support its autonomous driving R&D and made it a self-operated subsidiary this year. After this fundraiser, WeRide directly holds about 67.6 percent of Jingshuo, retaining control.

Jingshuo's Chief Executive Officer Huo Da was WeRide's first employee. The unit has engineering and R&D teams in the United States, China, and Singapore.

Editor: Futura Costaglione

data.title: Unitree Drops as Profit Shrinks 17%, R&D Expenses Surge 250% in Third Quarter
data.description:
(Yicai) Oct. 29 -- Shares of Unitree Robotics fell after the Chinese humanoid robot maker said its net profit declined over 17 percent in the third quarter, as research and development expenses skyrocketed 250 percent to support its embodied artificial intelligence efforts.

Unitree [SHA: 688836] was trading down 4.3 percent at CNY666 (USD99.97) as of lunch break in Shanghai today. The stock, which got listed on Aug. 19 with an initial public offering price of CNY150.80, reached a peak of CNY1,100 (USD165.11) per share on its debut, then fell to a low of CNY404.03 apiece on Oct. 15.

Net profit was CNY112.7 million (USD16.9 million) in the three months ended Sept. 30, down 17 percent from a year earlier, the Hangzhou-based company said in its latest financial statement released yesterday. Revenue rose 70 percent to CNY665 million, driven by continued product innovation, business expansion, and a broader product portfolio that better meets customer needs.

R&D expenses climbed 250 percent to CNY127 million in the period, accounting for 19 percent of the total revenue. This was mainly because of increased embodied AI investment, particularly in embodied AI foundation models and computing resources, an expanded R&D team, and new product development.

In the first three quarters, Unitree’s revenue jumped 56 percent to CNY1.8 billion (USD272.7 million), and its net profit grew 271 percent from a year earlier. However, net profit excluding non-recurring gains and losses shrank 19 percent to CNY349 million. R&D expenses surged 191 percent to CNY263 million in the period.

Unitree allocated CNY2 billion of the IPO proceeds, nearly half of the total, to an intelligent robot model R&D project. Founder Wang Xingxing said in August that AI model development was the company's largest area of investment in terms of both funds and personnel.

Unitree repeatedly warned in its IPO prospectus that market competition is intensifying. Reports from International Data Corporation and Smart Analytics Global showed that AgiBot shipped more humanoid robots than Unitree in the first half of the year.

On Oct. 26, Unitree issued a warning of abnormal stock movements, after the cumulative deviation in its share price gains exceeded 30 percent over three consecutive trading days. As of Oct. 26, its trailing price-to-earnings ratio stood at 465, compared with an average of 38.5 for the general equipment manufacturing industry in the previous month, according to China Securities Index.

The humanoid robot industry remains at an early stage of commercialization, with uncertainties surrounding technological maturity, downstream demand, and supply-chain capabilities, Unitree said. Moving physical AI from laboratory demonstrations to large-scale deployment in real-world scenarios still presents challenges, including perception accuracy, motion-control stability, data accumulation, and hardware-software integration.

If large-scale commercialization progresses more slowly than expected, Unitree’s earnings growth could be adversely affected, creating a risk of valuation correction, the firm noted.

Editor: Futura Costaglione

data.title: China’s Geely, Nio Strengthen Battery-Swap Alliance With Cross-Shareholding Deal
data.description:
(Yicai) Sept. 28 -- Chinese automotive giant Geely Holding Group and electric vehicle manufacturer Nio will deepen their strategic cooperation on battery swapping and EV charging through a cross-shareholding arrangement at the subsidiary level, aimed at accelerating the expansion of their battery-swap and charging service networks.

Geely will use its 100 percent equity in its battery-swap service provider Yiyi Internet Technology and CNY640 million (USD95.3 million) in cash to subscribe to newly issued shares in Nio’s battery-swap and charging unit Nio Power, Shanghai-based Nio said today. Upon completion of the transaction, Geely will hold a 30 percent stake in Nio Power, which will have a post-investment valuation of CNY16 billion (USD2.4 billion).

Nio was one of the earliest Chinese EV manufacturers to adopt battery swapping and set up Nio Power in 2017 to develop and run a battery-swap and charging service network. As of Sept. 20, Nio operated 4,099 battery-swap stations and 5,289 charging stations, and had provided users with over 120 million battery swaps in total, it said.

Yiyi, founded in 2017, managed more than 470 battery-swap stations in over 40 cities across China as of April last year, and has plans to expand to 2,000 stations by next year, according to its website.

The integration of Yiyi into Nio Power will accelerate the expansion of Nio's battery swapping network, with the aim of building 10,000 battery-swap stations by 2030, Nio said. The two sides will also work together to establish unified battery-swapping technology standards, while Hangzhou-based Geely will develop battery-swap vehicles models for consumers.

Nio will also acquire a stake in Geely’s EV charging service provider Zhejiang Haohan Energy Technology, according to the agreement between the two parties. Upon completion of the transaction, Nio will hold a 10 percent stake in Haohan, and both sides will share resources to expand charging network coverage and improve operational efficiency.

Haohan currently operates 2,500 charging stations and 12,000 charging guns in 232 cities across China. By the end of 2027, it plans to expand its network to 22,000 charging stations and 100,000 charging guns, Geely said.

The collaboration between Nio and Geely dates back to November 2023, when Nio announced plans to form a battery swapping alliance with automakers. Since then, it has established partnerships with eight automakers, including Changan Automobile and Geely.

Editor: Kim Taylor

data.title: China's DeepSeek Ranks First in Call Volume on OpenRouter for Third Straight Week
data.description:
(Yicai) Oct. 27 -- Models from DeepSeek, one of China's artificial intelligence champions, have topped the call volume ranking on application programming interface aggregation platform OpenRouter for the third week in a row, while Chinese AI models led US rivals for the 26th consecutive week.

DeepSeek's recently released V4.1-Flash-1017 ranked first with call volume at 33.6 trillion tokens in the week ended Oct. 25, followed by V4.1-Flash, according to data OpenRouter released yesterday. MiniMax-M3.1-Flash, Z.AI's GLM-5.3-Flash, and Tencent Hunyuan's Hy4 preview, all Chinese models, rounded out the top five.

Global LLM call volume on OpenRouter rose almost 15 percent to 188 trillion tokens week on week, while also surging from 5.51 trillion tokens a year ago. Among the top nine, Chinese AI models saw call volume jump 18 percent to 93.54 trillion tokens, while that of US counterparts logged a 29 percent increase to nearly 22.5 trillion tokens.

OpenRouter does not represent the entire AI model market, with its data counting only traffic routed through the platform and excluding vendors' own application programming interfaces, cloud platforms, on-premises deployments, consumer-facing apps, and web products. This means the figures cannot be directly equated with global market share.

In addition, a larger share of call volume for Chinese models does not necessarily mean they are generating more revenue, with overseas models still holding a clear lead in OpenRouter's spending share across different tasks. In the overall market structure, general-purpose tasks remain the core segment, accounting for 32 percent of spending, followed by Agent workflows at 31 percent and code-related tasks at 27 percent.

Classification is an important general-purpose task in which models need to identify the category of a given request, such as recognizing customer service intents, tagging documents, or determining which workflow a request should enter. In this task, Anthropic's Claude Opus 5.5 ranked first with a 10.3 percent share, followed by OpenAI's GPT-5.6 Sol and Google's Gemini 3.1 Pro, while V4.1-Flash was the only Chinese model on the list.

Chinese model providers have already used cost-effectiveness to capture traffic entry points and enter more users' workflows, but whether they can turn tokens into revenue and achieve higher profits still depends on actual payment conversion and inference costs. In addition, their models still lag in the ability to reliably complete more difficult tasks. With stronger capabilities, they would also gain greater pricing power.

Editor: Martin Kadiev
